brief: Create an original, warm, funny short conversation in natural, everyday Japanese between a married couple (or a couple living together) about one relatable daily-life moment — a 夫婦あるある that Japanese viewers instantly recognise. Choose a fresh topic and angle each run, and vary topics across runs. Draw from a broad mix: housework and who does what, meals and cooking, bath order and routines, money and small spending, days off and how each spends them, coming home late, misheard words and small misunderstandings, smartphones and TV habits, seasons and weather, neighbourhood and shopping, family visits, anniversaries and small celebrations, apologising and making up, and the small kindnesses that keep a marriage warm. Use natural, conversational Japanese with real lived detail (満員電車, コンビニ, お風呂の順番, ご飯・お風呂・寝る, etc.) — never stiff textbook Japanese or direct translations of English phrases. Keep it wholesome and funny, never toxic drama, blame, or stereotyping. Keep dialogue natural and concise, with a gentle punchline or warm ending. Write all dialogue, titles, and labels in Japanese.
